90:   "decodeURIComponent", "setTimeout", "setInterval", "clearTimeout", "clearInterval",
91:   "requestAnimationFrame", "require", "module", "exports", "process",

94: const JS_KEYWORDS = [

96:   "var", "new", "true", "false", "null", "undefined", "this", "typeof",
97:   "instanceof", "in", "of", "switch", "case", "break", "continue", "default",

100: ];

102: // Members accessed on p5 instances (p5.Element, p5.Vector, p5.Image) and on
103: // plain JS objects/arrays returned by the loaded data.
104: const MEMBER_ALLOWLIST = [
105:   // p5.Element
106:   "value", "checked", "color", "style", "size", "position", "elt", "id",
107:   "attribute", "removeAttribute", "addClass", "removeClass", "hasClass", "toggleClass",

110:   // p5.Vector

112:   "heading", "setHeading", "rotate", "dist", "dot", "cross", "lerp", "random2D",
113:   "random3D", "fromAngle", "copy", "array", "equals", "set", "get",
114:   // p5.Image / p5.Graphics
115:   "loadPixels", "updatePixels", "pixels", "set", "get", "width", "height",
116:   "copy", "resize", "mask", "filter", "blend", "save",
117:   // loaded-data / plain JS objects & arrays

119:   "toLowerCase", "push", "pop", "slice", "map", "filter", "reduce", "length",
120:   "x", "y", "z",
121: ];

123: function stripIgnored(src) {
124:   let out = "";
125:   let i = 0;
126:   const n = src.length;
127:   while (i < n) {
128:     const c = src[i], c2 = src[i + 1];
129:     if (c === "/" && c2 === "/") { while (i < n && src[i] !== "\n") i++; continue; }
130:     if (c === "/" && c2 === "*") { i += 2; while (i < n && !(src[i] === "*" && src[i + 1] === "/")) i++; i += 2; continue; }
131:     if (c === '"' || c === "'" || c === "`") {
132:       const q = c; i++;
133:       while (i < n) {
134:         if (src[i] === "\\") { i += 2; continue; }
135:         if (src[i] === q) { i++; break; }
136:         i++;
137:       }
138:       continue;
139:     }
140:     out += c; i++;
141:   }
142:   return out;
143: }
144: 
145: let symbolSet = new Set([...CORE_P5_SYMBOLS, ...JS_GLOBALS, ...JS_KEYWORDS]);
146: let refSymbols = new Set();

157: const callRe = /(?<![\w$.])\b([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(/g;
158: const memberRe = /\.([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\b/g;
159: const constRe = /\b([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\b/g;

161: function declaredNames(code) {
162:   const names = new Set();
163:   let m;
164:   const fnRe = /function\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/g;
165:   while ((m = fnRe.exec(code)) !== null) names.add(m[1]);
166:   const varRe = /\b(?:let|const|var)\s+([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)/g;
167:   while ((m = varRe.exec(code)) !== null) names.add(m[1]);
168:   const paramRe = /function\s*\(([^)]*)\)/g;
169:   while ((m = paramRe.exec(code)) !== null) {
170:     for (const p of m[1].split(",")) {
171:       const id = p.trim().split(/[=:]/)[0].trim();
172:       if (/^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(id)) names.add(id);
173:     }
174:   }
175:   return names;
176: }
177: 
178: let failures = 0;
179: function report(file, exId, block, msg) {
180:   console.error(`  ✗ ${file} ${exId} ${block}: ${msg}`);
181:   failures++;
182: }
183: 
184: const yamlFiles = fs.readdirSync(COURSES_DIR).filter((f) => f.endsWith(".yaml") || f.endsWith(".yml"));
185:

188:   for (const ex of course.exercises ?? []) {
189:     const blocks = [

191:       ["solution", ex.solution],
192:       ...(ex.tasks ?? []).map((t) => [`task.${t.id}.solution`, t.solution]),
193:     ];
194:     for (const [label, src] of blocks) {
195:       if (!src) continue;
196:       const code = stripIgnored(src);
197:       const declared = declaredNames(code);
198:       let m;
199:       callRe.lastIndex = 0;
200:       while ((m = callRe.exec(code)) !== null) {
201:         const name = m[1];
202:         if (!symbolSet.has(name) && !declared.has(name)) {
203:           report(file, ex.id, label, `unknown function call ${name}()`);
204:         }
205:       }
206:       memberRe.lastIndex = 0;
207:       while ((m = memberRe.exec(code)) !== null) {
208:         const name = m[1];
209:         if (!symbolSet.has(name) && !MEMBER_ALLOWLIST.includes(name) && !declared.has(name)) {
210:           report(file, ex.id, label, `unknown member .${name}`);
211:         }
212:       }
213:       constRe.lastIndex = 0;
214:       while ((m = constRe.exec(code)) !== null) {
215:         const name = m[1];
216:         if (!P5_CONSTANTS.includes(name) && !refSymbols.has(name) && !JS_GLOBALS.includes(name)) {
217:           report(file, ex.id, label, `unknown constant ${name}`);
218:         }
219:       }
220:     }
221:   }
222: }
223: 
224: if (failures > 0) {
225:   console.error(`\n${failures} unknown symbol(s) in course YAML.`);
226:   process.exit(1);
227: } else {
228:   console.log("All course YAML symbols resolve to known p5/JS symbols.");
229: }

27:     { encoding: "utf-8", maxBuffer: 50 * 1024 * 1024 }
28:   );

parts.text:
Good. Now I have a comprehensive understanding. Let me now consider the approach and present the plan.

Key facts:
- Node 24, npm 11.
- @lezer/javascript installed (used by check-exercises to feed the validation core).
- esbuild + tsc available.
- No jest/vitest installed.
- AGENTS.md: never run npm install on dev machine; only edit package.json; user installs.
- Version bump workflow via pre-push hook: any push to main must bump version + tag. But test additions are usually pushed via normal workflow. That's for when pushing; not our immediate concern.

Testing framework decision. Options:

**Option A: Vitest (recommended)**
- Add `vitest` as devDependency.
- Pros: TS out of the box, fast, first-class mocking (vi.mock for AsyncStorage), watch mode, easy config in vite.config.ts or vitest.config.ts, works with ESM modules and JSON imports. Can also test React hook logic with @testing-library/react if desired (but that adds more deps). For pure logic + AsyncStorage-mocked hook functions (recordCompletion, checkStreak are exported plain async functions — no need for react rendering!), vitest alone suffices.
- Notably: useAchievements.ts exports `recordCompletion` as a plain async function (not a hook) — perfect for unit testing without react-test-renderer. useStreak exports `checkStreak` via the hook but the pure logic (getCurrentTierIndex, dateKey) is internal. However, the exported `getStreakFromStorage` is a plain function. The streak logic could be tested by extracting... hmm, we can't easily test `checkStreak` without rendering the hook, unless we refactor. Actually useStreak is a React hook — testing it requires renderHook from @testing-library/react + react-test-renderer. That's heavier. We could either:
  - Test only exported non-hook functions (getStreakFromStorage, STREAK_TIERS, getUnlockedAchievements, getUnlockedAchievementsAt, recordCompletion) — these are real logic.
  - OR do a small refactor to extract the streak transition logic into a pure function `computeStreakTransition(prevCount, lastVisit, today)` in a new module `src/utils/streak.ts`, then useStreak calls it. This improves testability (a refactor worth doing) — but plan mode; I can propose it as part of the plan.

  Actually a cleaner approach: refactor the date/business logic out of hooks into pure utils. But that increases scope. Let me weigh: the user asked to "write tests for the app to detect regressions as we improve the app." Testing the pure logic modules (validation core, color utils, isExerciseLocked, referenceRender text functions, exampleHtml, courseLoader integrity, achievements recordCompletion, streak helpers) is the high-value, low-risk core. For hooks, we can test their exported plain functions and mock AsyncStorage. Optionally add @testing-library/react-native later.

**Option B: Jest + jest-expo**
- Expo-recommended; matches SDK 55. But heavier config, slower, and RN module mocks needed. Only worth it if testing components/rendering. Overkill for now.

**Option C: node:test with esbuild-bundled tests**
- Zero new deps but very manual (build each test file, JSON imports need handling, AsyncStorage mocking manual). Poor DX, more custom infra to maintain.

I'll recommend Vitest. It's a single devDependency, fast, and handles TS/ESM/JSON/mocking cleanly. Given AGENTS.md constraint, I'll edit package.json to add vitest and a `test` script; the user runs `npm install`.

Now, which files to test (the "regression detection" value):

1. **Validation core** (`src/utils/editor/validation.ts`) — highest value. Tests:
   - `analyze`: 
     - detects plain calls (name, args count)
     - member calls (e.g., `vec.add(1,2)` → name `add`, member true)
     - createCanvas captures width/height, canvasPresent
     - createCanvas with expressions/undefined returns canvasPresent true, canvas null
     - functionDefs from function declarations, arrow functions assigned to const/let/var, object methods, class methods
     - nested call expressions, arg counting ignores separators and `...`
     - new expressions (e.g., `new p5.Vector()`)
   - `evaluateRules`:
     - functionCall pass/fail, exactArgs, minArgs
     - functionExists
     - canvasSize
     - pixel rules skipped (returned passed)
     - reason strings
   - `schemaErrors`:
     - unknown rule type, missing required fields, unknown fields, bad field types, points validation
     - valid rules produce no errors
   - `pixelMatches`, `effectiveTolerance`, `effectiveMinPassFraction`, `hasPixelRules`, `hasSyncRules`
   - RULE_SCHEMAS completeness
   - Adapter: use @lezer/javascript `parser.parse(code)` with `cursor()` + slice — same as check-exercises.

2. **Color utils** (`src/utils/colorUtils.ts`):
   - rgbToHex / hexToRgb round trips, clamping
   - hslToRgb / rgbToHsl round trips on known values
   - luminance known values (e.g., black 0, white 1, mid grays)
   - contrastRatio (black vs white = 21)
   - bestOnColor threshold
   - deriveColorsFromAccent: dark vs light, primary === accent, all hex format, invariants (valid #rrggbb, onPrimary contrast), no NaN, deterministic
   - deriveAccentShades: all valid hex, medium === accent

3. **isExerciseLocked**: pure — first exercise unlocked, locked when prior incomplete, unlocked when prior completed, unknown id not locked, etc.

4. **referenceRender** text functions: `extractDescribeCaption`, `stripDescribe`, `highlightSyntax` (tokenization doesn't throw, covers strings/comments/numbers/keywords/functions; reconstructing text equals input). These are pure (module imports react-native Text but the functions don't use it; under vitest, importing react-native may or may not work — we can test just these functions; if RN import is problematic, we can still import since vitest will just load the module; `react-native` imports index.js which imports lots of stuff... risky. Might need a mock. Actually react-native 0.83 — importing it in Node without jest-expo transform... `react-native` package main is `index.js` which requires RN internals; under vitest with default node environment it may fail. We can add `vi.mock('react-native', () => ({ Text: () => null }))` at the top of the test file — that intercepts the import before module load. That works with vitest's module mocking even for CJS. Good.)
   
   Alternatively test `parseInstructionHtml`-equivalent. But parseDescription returns React nodes — skip or light-test.

5. **exampleHtml getExampleHtml**: 
   - wraps code lacking `function setup` into a setup() with createCanvas(400,400)
   - replaces createCanvas dims with 400x400 when setup present
   - asset placeholder substitution
   - escaping (can't easily test output HTML details but can test contains `<script>${p5Source}</script>` etc.)
   - Imports p5Source (big) + p5Assets.generated.json (big) — import time heavy but OK. Colors.ts is pure. fontBase64.generated — big strings. This is fine under vitest.

6. **courseLoader / course data integrity**:
   - 16 courses, unique slugs, non-empty titles
   - unique exercise ids within each course and across courses (the completedLessons use `${courseSlug}/${exerciseId}` so collisions across courses would be a bug!)
   - every exercise has required fields
   - moduleName present
   - tasks have ids, validation rules well-formed (schemaErrors empty) — though check-exercises already covers solutions vs rules. But a data integrity test in the test suite is valuable and fast.
   - No duplicate exercise ids across courses.

7. **useAchievements.recordCompletion** (mock AsyncStorage):
   - first completion → "first-strokes"
   - 3 events same day → "daily-3"
   - quickdraw when durationMs < 30000
   - on-a-roll when 3 events within 10 min
   - weekender when streak_count >= 7 in storage
   - de-dup: same exercise same day not double counted
   - idempotency: unlocked set not returned twice
   - getUnlockedAchievements returns stored

8. **useStreak / streak logic**: 
   - STREAK_TIERS and tier index computation (getCurrentTierIndex is internal). Optionally propose extracting pure function. 
   - `getStreakFromStorage` with mocked AsyncStorage.
   - If we want deeper coverage of checkStreak (new-day increments, consecutive vs reset, longest), we could refactor the transition logic into a pure exported helper. I'll propose a minimal, low-risk extraction: add `src/utils/streakLogic.ts` with `computeStreakDay(lastVisit, today, prevCount, prevLongest)` returning {count, longest, isNewDay}. Then useStreak uses it, and tests cover it thoroughly. This is a behavior-preserving refactor. But it changes app code — slightly more risk. Alternative: test only what's exported. Hmm.

   Given "detect regressions as we improve the app", the streak logic is important (user retention). I think extracting pure logic is worth it and low-risk. But I should flag it in the plan as an optional refactor, and get user buy-in.

9. **p5Version / Version constants**: trivial snapshot tests maybe not worth it. Skip.

10. **check-exercises / check-symbols** already exist as invariants. We could also add a test that runs them? Not necessary. But we might add a regression test asserting course YAML count matches generated .ts files? Actually the build copies YAML→TS. A data-integrity test on courseLoader (which reads the generated .ts) is enough.

Test infrastructure plan:
- Add `vitest` devDependency (`^3.x` latest compatible) to package.json.
- Add `"test": "vitest run"` and maybe `"test:watch": "vitest"` scripts. Possibly `"test:coverage"`? Might add @vitest/coverage-v8 — extra dep. Keep optional.
- Create `vitest.config.ts` with:
  - environment: 'node'
  - globals: false (or true; prefer explicit imports: `import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest'`)
  - resolve alias `@` → `./src`

#!/usr/bin/env sh
# Pre-push hook (Husky).
# 1) Push Entire CLI session logs alongside the user's push.
# 2) Enforce that a push to main includes a version bump in package.json
#    AND a matching vX.Y.Z tag (see AGENTS.md "Release cadence").

# 1) Entire CLI session-log hook (no-op if the CLI is unavailable).
if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  entire hooks git pre-push "$1" || true
fi

# 2) Version-bump enforcement.
while read -r local_ref local_sha remote_ref remote_sha; do
  [ "$local_ref" = "refs/heads/main" ] || continue

  if [ -z "$remote_sha" ] || [ "$remote_sha" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
    range="$local_sha"
  else
    range="$remote_sha..$local_sha"
  fi

  repo_dir=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)

  bumped_version=""
  if git diff --name-only "$range" -- "$repo_dir/package.json" 2>/dev/null | grep -q package.json; then
    bumped_version=$(git show "$local_sha:package.json" 2>/dev/null | node -e "
      let data='';
      process.stdin.on('data',c=>data+=c);
      process.stdin.on('end',()=>{
        try { process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(data).version || ''); }
        catch(e) { process.stdout.write(''); }
      });
    ")
  fi

  if [ -z "$bumped_version" ]; then
    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: push to main must include a version bump in package.json." >&2
    echo "           Run: sh scripts/bump-version.sh  then commit, then:" >&2
    echo "           git tag v0.6.<next>  before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if ! git rev-parse -q --verify "refs/tags/v$bumped_version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "[pre-push] ERROR: package.json is at $bumped_version but tag v$bumped_version does not exist locally." >&2
    echo "           Run: git tag v$bumped_version  before pushing." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

exit 0

`@lezer/javascript` has TypeScript types (dist/index.d.ts). So a TS test can import it directly.

Now, let me check what vitest version to use. Latest vitest 3.x. Node 24 supports it. I'll suggest `vitest ^3.2.4` (or whatever latest 3.x).

Now let me verify the testability of `useAchievements`/`useStreak` imports. They import `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage` (CJS). Vitest can mock with `vi.mock('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage', ...)`. Good.

Now the `referenceRender.tsx` imports `react-native` (for `Text`) and `./editor/themes` (pure). Under vitest node env, importing `react-native` will fail because RN requires `global.navigator`/native modules? Actually react-native's index.js in Node throws or warns; importing `Text` from 'react-native' in a node env typically errors with "Cannot find module 'react-native/Libraries/...'". We can `vi.mock('react-native', ...)` before importing the module. In vitest, `vi.mock` is hoisted, so if we call `vi.mock('react-native', () => ({ Text: ... }))` at the top of the test file, the subsequent `import { highlightSyntax } from '../../referenceRender'` gets the mocked RN. But ES imports are hoisted above `vi.mock` calls in source order... Vitest handles this by hoisting `vi.mock` calls to the top of the file (they're transformed). Actually `vi.mock` is hoisted to the top regardless of position. So it works. This is standard.

But do we even need referenceRender tests? The highlightSyntax tokenizer is real logic used in reference rendering. A regression test that highlights a complex snippet and verifies round-trip (concatenating token.text === original code) plus specific token classification (e.g., a comment token colored as comment) is valuable and cheap. And stripDescribe/extractDescribeCaption are used in exercise flow. I'll include them.

For exampleHtml tests: imports p5Source (1MB string), p5Assets.generated.json (2.9MB), fontBase64.generated (huge base64). Loading all these into memory for tests is fine (they're already loaded by the app). Tests: 
- needsWrap when no setup function
- replaces createCanvas dims when setup present
- substitutes asset placeholders
- HTML escapes in sketch? Not really.
- Colors injected.

Actually wait — exampleHtml imports `../../constants/fontBase64.generated` — that's a `.ts` generated file with base64 strings. It's 964KB-ish. Fine.

For p5Source test: p5Source.ts is generated; importing it is fine.

Course data integrity tests: import courseLoader → imports all course .ts files (compiled from YAML). These .ts files exist (generated). They import `../types`. Good. Test:
- loadAllCourses returns 16 courses
- unique slugs, unique exercise ids (across all courses — important for the `${courseSlug}/${exerciseId}` key scheme)
- each exercise has id/title/module/instruction, startingCode or tasks
- each task has id + validation + schemaErrors([]) — a data-level schema check
- each exercise's schemaErrors empty too? exercises don't have validation at top-level; tasks do.

Now, one consideration: course .ts files are gitignored artifacts regenerated on postinstall/start. Tests depend on them existing (they do exist in this workspace). That's consistent with check-exercises which requires validation-core.generated.ts to exist. We should note in the plan that `npm run build-courses` must have been run (postinstall does it). The test script could optionally run build-courses first? Better not — keep tests pure; just document the dependency. Actually to make `npm test` robust, we could make the test script `npm run build-courses && vitest run`? That would slow things. Or leave as documented dependency since postinstall runs it. I'll note it.

Streak logic: I want deeper coverage. Options:
(a) Test only exported functions: STREAK_TIERS, getStreakFromStorage (with mocked AsyncStorage).

          \            include "arm64-v8a", "armeabi-v7a"\
          \            universalApk false\
          \        }\
          \    }' android/app/build.gradle

      - name: Build release APKs (per ABI)
        run: cd android && ./gradlew assembleRelease

      - name: List split APKs

          done

      - name: Upload split APKs to release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: android/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk

Not our concern for the plan, though note that adding package.json devDependency will trigger the version-bump requirement on the next push to main (standard workflow).

Let me decide the vitest version: latest stable vitest 3.x (3.2.x). Since Node is 24, vitest 3 requires Node 18+. Good. The `@vitest/coverage-v8` optional.

Now, one question: does vitest handle importing `*.tsx` files with JSX in node environment? Vitest transforms with esbuild, so JSX transpiles fine. The `react-native` import needs mocking. And `react` import in referenceRender? No, referenceRender only imports react-native and data. `renderHighlightedCode` returns React nodes but doesn't import react. OK.

For exampleHtml.ts: imports `../../constants/fontBase64.generated` (a .ts with const base64 strings). Fine.

For useAchievements.test.ts: `vi.mock('@react-native-async-storage/async-storage', ...)`. Provide an in-memory implementation. Since `recordCompletion` reads/writes with getItem/setItem and the mock needs to persist across calls in the same test. We'll implement a simple map-based mock. Provide a helper `src/test/asyncStorageMock.ts` exporting `createAsyncStorageMock()` returning `{ storage, mock }` and `resetStorage()`.

Actually there's a subtlety: `recordCompletion` uses `Date.now()` and `new Date()` for today's bucket and timestamps. For deterministic tests of "daily-3" and "on-a-roll", we need to control time. We can use `vi.useFakeTimers()` with `vi.setSystemTime(...)`. But the code computes `today` via `dateKey(Date.now())` inside recordCompletion, and ts uses Date.now(). With fake timers, Date.now() is controlled. Good. For on-a-roll (3 events in 10 min), we need multiple completions across different timestamps but same day. With fake timers we can advance time. But note: the de-dup check is per exerciseId per day. So for on-a-roll test, use different exerciseIds, each completion with advanced fake time. Also quickdraw: durationMs < 30000.

But careful: with fake timers + `await AsyncStorage` promises, fake timers can cause issues with promise resolution. Use `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })` to only fake Date, leaving timers real. That's the clean approach: `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ['Date'] })`. Vitest supports that. Good — the plan should note this.

Alternatively use `vi.setSystemTime`. Same thing.

For streak logic: to test `checkStreak` without rendering the hook, we need a pure extraction OR just test `getStreakFromStorage` (trivial). I'll propose extracting pure helpers. Let me design:

Create `src/utils/streakLogic.ts`:
```ts
export const STREAK_TIERS = [3, 7, 14, 30, 100, 365];
export function getCurrentTierIndex(days) {...}
export function computeStreakTransition(args: { lastVisit: string|null, today: string, yesterday: string, prevCount: number, prevLongest: number }) 
  -> { newCount: number; newLongest: number; isNewDay: boolean }
```
Then `useStreak` imports STREAK_TIERS and computeStreakTransition. Tests cover:
- first visit (no lastVisit) → count 1, isNewDay true
- consecutive yesterday → count+1
- same day → isNewDay false, count unchanged
- gap (lastVisit older) → count resets to 1
- longest tracking
- tier index boundaries (2→-1/0, 3→0, 6→0, 7→1, 13→1, 14→2, 365→5, 366→5)
- tierProgress edge (count >= last tier → progress 1)

This refactor is small and low-risk. But it modifies app code. I'll flag it in the plan and ask the user whether they want the refactor or just test exported surface.

Actually — let me reconsider. The instruction says "write tests for the app to detect regressions as we improve the app." Testing should primarily use existing public surface to minimize risk. But the streak logic is currently locked inside a hook, meaning it can't be unit-tested without react test renderer. Two options: add @testing-library/react (renderHook) — heavier; or extract pure logic. I think extraction is cleaner and I'll present it. But I could also test via the exported `useStreak` using `react-test-renderer`? Not installed. Let me keep it as an explicit decision point in the plan.

Actually, let me limit scope creep. The plan will:
- Core: pure-logic test suites (no app code changes).
- Optional (recommended): extract streak pure logic (tiny, safe).
- Optional: `getStreakFromStorage` test (no changes).

Let me now also verify the exact behavior of the date-key/today logic in achievements for testability. Fine.

One more: `isExerciseLocked` — note the loop over `j < idx` requires ALL prior exercises completed. Interesting edge: if idx>0 and any prior incomplete → locked. Tests:
- empty completed → exercise 1 unlocked, exercise 2 locked
- completed first → exercise 2 unlocked
- completed second only → exercise 3 still locked
- id not in list → unlocked (idx -1 → idx<=0 → false)
- courseSlug prefix matching (completedLessons entries are `${courseSlug}/${id}`)
- cross-course: completing shapes/exercise-1 doesn't unlock transform/exercise-2.

Vitest + `@lezer/javascript` ESM: vitest handles it.

Now the test for validation-core bundle sync: 
```ts
import { analyze as srcAnalyze, evaluateRules as srcEval, schemaErrors as srcSchema } from '../validation';
import { VALIDATION_CORE } from '../validation-core.generated';
// eval
new Function(VALIDATION_CORE)();
const core = (globalThis as any).__VAL_CORE;
// compare behaviors across a battery of (code, rules) pairs
```
The generated file exists (6733 bytes). It imports from validation-core.generated.ts which just exports a string. Good.

But hold on — do we want a test that fails when the bundle is stale? That requires the source and bundle to agree. If a dev edits validation.ts but doesn't run bundle-validation, the test fails (good, detects regression). But the test file imports both modules at top; eval of VALIDATION_CORE sets globalThis.__VAL_CORE — fine in node env.

## Plan: Regression test suite for learn-p5

### Goal
Add a fast, Node-based unit test suite covering the app's core logic to catch regressions during ongoing improvements.

### Framework
Recommend Vitest (v3.x). One devDependency. TS/TSX via esbuild (already in stack), first-class mocking for AsyncStorage, fake timers for date logic, no RN transform needed for pure modules. # Unit testing with Jest

Learn how to set up and configure the jest-expo library to write unit and snapshot tests for a project with Jest.

[Jest](https://jestjs.io) is the most widely used unit and snapshot JavaScript testing framework. In this guide, you will learn how to set up Jest in your project, write a unit test, write a snapshot test, and best practices for structuring your tests when using Jest with React Native.

You will also use the [`jest-expo`](https://github.com/expo/expo/tree/main/packages/jest-expo) library, which is a Jest preset that mocks the native part of the Expo SDK and handles most of the configuration required for your Expo project.

## Installation and configuration

After creating your Expo project, follow the instructions below to install and configure `jest-expo` in your project:

Install `jest-expo` and other required dev dependencies in your project. Run the following command from your project's root directory:

#### macOS/Linux

```sh
# npm
npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest --dev

# yarn
yarn expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest --dev

# pnpm
pnpm expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest --dev

# bun
bun expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest --dev
```

#### Windows

```sh
# npm
npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest "--" --dev

# yarn
yarn expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest "--" --dev

# pnpm
pnpm expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest "--" --dev

# bun
bun expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest "--" --dev
```

> **Note:** If your project is not using TypeScript, you can skip installing `@types/jest`.

If your project uses TypeScript, add `"jest"` to the `types` array in your **tsconfig.json** to enable Jest's type definitions:

```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "types": ["jest"]
  }
}
```

Open **package.json**, add a script for running tests, and add the preset for using the base configuration from `jest-expo`:

```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "test": "jest --watchAll"
    ...
```

In **package.json**, add `jest-expo` as a preset so that a base for Jest's configuration is set up:

```json
{
  "jest": {
    "preset": "jest-expo"
  }
}
```

#### Additional configuration for using transformIgnorePatterns

You can transpile node modules your project uses by configuring [`transformIgnorePatterns`](https://jestjs.io/docs/configuration#transformignorepatterns-arraystring) in your **package.json**. This property takes a regex pattern as its value:

#### npm/Yarn

```json
"jest": {
  "preset": "jest-expo",
  "transformIgnorePatterns": [
    "node_modules/(?!((jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?)|expo(nent)?|@expo(nent)?/.*|@expo-google-fonts/.*|react-navigation|@react-navigation/.*|@sentry/react-native|native-base|react-native-svg)"
  ]
}
```

#### pnpm

```json
"jest": {
  "preset": "jest-expo",
  "transformIgnorePatterns": [
    "node_modules/(?!(.pnpm|(jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?|expo(nent)?|@expo(nent)?/.*|@expo-google-fonts/.*|react-navigation|@react-navigation/.*|@sentry/react-native|native-base|react-native-svg))"
  ]
}
```

#### Bun

```json
"jest": {
  "preset": "jest-expo",
  "transformIgnorePatterns": [
    "node_modules/(?!(.bun|(jest-)?react-native|@react-native(-community)?|expo(nent)?|@expo(nent)?/.*|@expo-google-fonts/.*|react-navigation|@react-navigation/.*|@sentry/react-native|native-base|react-native-svg))"
  ]
}
```

Jest has many configuration options, but the above configuration should cover most of your needs. However, you can always add to this pattern list. For more details, see [Configuring Jest](https://jestjs.io/docs/configuration).

## Install React Native Testing Library

The [React Native Testing Library (`@testing-library/react-native`)](https://callstack.github.io/react-native-testing-library/) is a lightweight solution for testing React Native components. It provides utility functions and works with Jest.

To install it, run the following command:

#### macOS/Linux

```sh
# npm
npx expo install @testing-library/react-native --dev

# yarn
yarn expo install @testing-library/react-native --dev

# pnpm
pnpm expo install @testing-library/react-native --dev

# bun
bun expo install @testing-library/react-native --dev
```

#### Windows

```sh
# npm
npx expo install @testing-library/react-native "--" --dev

# yarn
yarn expo install @testing-library/react-native "--" --dev

# pnpm
pnpm expo install @testing-library/react-native "--" --dev

# bun
bun expo install @testing-library/react-native "--" --dev
```

> **[Deprecated](/more/release-statuses.md#deprecated):** `@testing-library/react-native` replaces the deprecated `react-test-renderer` because `react-test-renderer` does not support React 19 and above. Remove the deprecated library from your project if you are currently using it. See [React's documentation for more information](https://react.dev/warnings/react-test-renderer).

## Unit test

A unit test checks the smallest unit of code, usually a function. To write your first unit test, take a look at the following example:

Inside the **src/app** directory of your project, create a new file called **index.tsx**, and the following code to render a simple component:

```tsx
import { PropsWithChildren } from 'react';
import { StyleSheet, Text, View } from 'react-native';

export const CustomText = ({ children }: PropsWithChildren) => <Text>{children}</Text>;

export default function HomeScreen() {
  return (
    <View style={styles.container}>
      <CustomText>Welcome!</CustomText>
    </View>
  );
}

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  container: {
    flex: 1,
    backgroundColor: '#fff',
    alignItems: 'center',
    justifyContent: 'center',
  },
});
```

Create a **__tests__** directory at the root of your project's directory. If this directory already exists in your project, use that. Then, create a new file called **home-screen-test.tsx**. The `jest-expo` preset customizes the Jest configuration to also identify files with **-test.ts|tsx** extensions as tests.

Add the following example code in **home-screen-test.tsx**:

```tsx
import { render } from '@testing-library/react-native';

import HomeScreen, { CustomText } from '@/app/index';

describe('<HomeScreen />', () => {
  test('Text renders correctly on HomeScreen', async () => {
    const { getByText } = await render(<HomeScreen />);

    getByText('Welcome!');
  });
});
```

In the above example, the `getByText` query helps your tests find relevant element in your app's user interface and make assertion whether or not the certain element exists. The React Native Testing Library provides this query, and each [query variant](https://callstack.github.io/react-native-testing-library/docs/api/queries#query-variant) differs in its return type. For more examples and detailed API information, see the React Native Testing Library's [Queries API reference](https://callstack.github.io/react-native-testing-library/docs/api/queries).

Run the following command in a terminal window to execute the test:

```sh
# npm
npm run test

# yarn
yarn run test

# pnpm
pnpm run test

# bun
bun run test
```

You will see one test being passed.

## Structure your tests

Organizing your test files is important to make them easier to maintain. A common pattern is creating a **__tests__** directory and putting all your tests inside.

An example structure of tests next to the **components** directory is shown below:

`__tests__`

 `themed-text-test.tsx`

`src`

 `components`

  `themed-text.tsx`

  `themed-view.tsx`

Alternatively, you can have multiple **__tests__** sub-directories for different areas of your project. For example, create a separate test directory for **components**, and so on:

`src`

 `components`

  `themed-text.tsx`

  `__tests__`

   `themed-text-test.tsx`

 `utils`

  `index.tsx`

  `__tests__`

   `index-test.tsx`

It's all about preferences, and it is up to you to decide how you want to organize your project directory.

## Snapshot test

> **Note:** For UI testing, we recommend end-to-end tests instead of snapshot unit tests. See the [E2E tests with Maestro](/eas/workflows/examples/e2e-tests.md) guide.

A [snapshot test](https://jestjs.io/docs/en/snapshot-testing) is used to make sure that UI stays consistent, especially when a project is working with global styles that are potentially shared across components.

To add a snapshot test for `<HomeScreen />`, add the following code snippet in the `describe()` in **home-screen-test.tsx**:

```tsx
describe('<HomeScreen />', () => {
  ... 

  test('CustomText renders correctly', async () => {
    const tree = (await render(<CustomText>Some text</CustomText>)).toJSON();

    expect(tree).toMatchSnapshot();
  });
});
```

Run `npm run test` command, and you will see a snapshot created inside **__tests__\\__snapshots__** directory, and two tests passed.

## Code coverage reports

Code coverage reports can help you understand how much of your code is tested. To see the code coverage report in your project using the HTML format, in **package.json**, under `jest`, set the `collectCoverage` to true and use `collectCoverageFrom` to specify a list of files to ignore when collecting the coverage.

```json
"jest": {
  ...
  "collectCoverage": true,
  "collectCoverageFrom": [
    "**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx}",
    "!**/coverage/**",
    "!**/node_modules/**",
    "!**/babel.config.js",
    "!**/expo-env.d.ts",
    "!**/.expo/**"
  ]
}
```

Run `npm run test`. You will see a **coverage** directory created in your project. Find the **lcov-report/index.html** and open it in a browser to see the coverage report.

> Usually, we don't recommend uploading **index.html** file to git. Add `coverage/**/*` in the **.gitignore** file to prevent it from being tracked.

## Jest flows (optional)

You can also use different flows to run your tests. Below are a few example scripts that you can try:

```json
"scripts": {
  "test": "jest --watch --coverage=false --changedSince=origin/main",
  "testDebug": "jest -o --watch --coverage=false",
  "testFinal": "jest",
  "updateSnapshots": "jest -u --coverage=false"
  ... 
}
```

For more information, see [CLI Options](https://jestjs.io/docs/en/cli) in Jest documentation.

## Additional information

[React Native Testing library documentation](https://callstack.github.io/react-native-testing-library/docs/start/quick-start) — See React Native Testing Library documentation, which provides testing utilities and encourages good testing practices and work with Jest.

[Testing configuration for Expo Router](/router/reference/testing.md) — Learn how to create integration tests for your app when using Expo Router.

[E2E tests with EAS Workflows](/eas/workflows/examples/e2e-tests.md) — Learn how to set up and run E2E tests on EAS Workflows with Maestro.

83:     await AsyncStorage.setItem(EVENTS_KEY, JSON.stringify(events));
84:   }
85: 
86:   const unlockedRaw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(UNLOCKED_KEY);
87:   const unlocked: string[] = unlockedRaw ? JSON.parse(unlockedRaw) : [];
88:   const unlockedAtRaw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(UNLOCKED_AT_KEY);
89:   const unlockedAt: Record<string, string> = unlockedAtRaw ? JSON.parse(unlockedAtRaw) : {};
90:   const newlyUnlocked: string[] = [];
91: 
92:   function grant(id: string, predicate: () => boolean) {
93:     if (!unlocked.includes(id) && !newlyUnlocked.includes(id) && predicate()) {
94:       newlyUnlocked.push(id);
95:       unlocked.push(id);
96:       if (!unlockedAt[id]) unlockedAt[id] = new Date().toISOString();
97:     }
98:   }
99: 
100:   const todays = events.filter((e) => dateKey(e.ts) === today);
101: 
102:   grant("first-strokes", () => events.length >= 1);
103:   grant("daily-3", () => todays.length >= 3);
104:   grant("quickdraw", () => events.some((e) => (e.durationMs ?? Infinity) < 30000));
105: 
106:   // On a Roll: 3 events within any 10-minute window.
107:   grant("on-a-roll", () => {
108:     if (events.length < 3) return false;
109:     const sorted = [...events].sort((a, b) => a.ts - b.ts);
110:     for (let i = 2; i < sorted.length; i++) {
111:       if (sorted[i].ts - sorted[i - 2].ts <= 10 * 60 * 1000) return true;
112:     }
113:     return false;
114:   });
115: 
116:   // Weekender: streak >= 7. Read live so the badge can unlock the moment
117:   // the streak crosses the threshold, independent of completion timing.
118:   const streakCountStr = await AsyncStorage.getItem("streak_count");
119:   const streakCount = streakCountStr ? parseInt(streakCountStr, 10) : 0;
120:   grant("weekender", () => streakCount >= 7);
121: 
122:   // Backfill: any achievement unlocked before timestamps were tracked gets
123: // today's date so its badge modal can still show an "earned" date.
124:   let backfilled = false;
125:   for (const id of unlocked) {
126:     if (!unlockedAt[id]) {
127:       unlockedAt[id] = new Date().toISOString();
128:       backfilled = true;
129:     }
130:   }
131: 
132:   if (newlyUnlocked.length > 0 || backfilled) {
133:     await AsyncStorage.setItem(UNLOCKED_KEY, JSON.stringify(unlocked));
134:     await AsyncStorage.setItem(UNLOCKED_AT_KEY, JSON.stringify(unlockedAt));
135:   }
136: 
137:   return newlyUnlocked;
138: }
139: 
140: export async function getUnlockedAchievements(): Promise<string[]> {
141:   const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(UNLOCKED_KEY);
142:   return raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : [];
143: }
144: 
145: export async function getUnlockedAchievementsAt(): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
146:   const raw = await AsyncStorage.getItem(UNLOCKED_AT_KEY);
147:   return raw ? JSON.parse(raw) : {};
148: }
149: 
150: export function useAchievements() {
151:   const [unlocked, setUnlocked] = useState<string[]>([]);
152:   const [unlockedAt, setUnlockedAt] = useState<Record<string, string>>({});
153: 
154:   const refresh = useCallback(async () => {
155:     setUnlocked(await getUnlockedAchievements());
156:     setUnlockedAt(await getUnlockedAchievementsAt());
157:   }, []);
158: 
159:   useEffect(() => {
160:     refresh();
161:   }, [refresh]);
162: 
163:   return { unlocked, unlockedAt, refresh };
164: }

Done. The regression test suite is fully implemented and verified as far as possible without `npm install`.

## What changed

**Infrastructure**
- `package.json` — added `jest`, `jest-expo ~55.0.20`, `@types/jest`, `@testing-library/react-native ^14.0.1`, `test-renderer ^1.2.0` (RNTL 14's peer); `test`/`test:watch` scripts; root `jest` block with `preset: jest-expo`, `setupFilesAfterEnv: [jest.setup.js]`, and transformIgnorePatterns replicating jest-expo 55.0.20's exact defaults (verified from the npm tarball) plus `@lezer`.
- `jest.setup.js` — reanimated `setUpTests()`, gesture-handler jestSetup, safe-area-context mock, AsyncStorage mock, and a react-native-svg host-component mock (svg ships no jest mock).

**Behavior-preserving refactor**
- `src/utils/streakLogic.ts` (new): `STREAK_TIERS`, `getCurrentTierIndex`, `getTierInfo`, `computeStreakTransition`.
- `src/hooks/useStreak.ts` consumes the helpers; diffed against `HEAD` — identical runtime behavior; `STREAK_TIERS` re-exported (StreakToast still imports it).
- `src/utils/colorUtils.ts` — added `export` to 7 pure helpers.

**21 test files** (10 logic + 8 component + 3 helpers): validation core, bundle↔source parity, colorUtils, isExerciseLocked, referenceRender, exampleHtml, courseLoader, streakLogic, useStreak, useAchievements, plus Button, Breadcrumbs, ModuleCover, ExerciseCard, Header, DrawerContext, ThemeProvider, StatusBarAccent.

## Verification (run)
- `tsc --noEmit` (throwaway /tmp config stubbing the two uninstalled packages) — clean
- Runtime bundle↔source parity battery (esbuild) — PARITY OK
- `npm run check-exercises` and `npm run check-symbols` — both pass
- ESLint on changed app files — clean

## Notes
- **You need to run `npm install`**, then `npm test` (I can't install per your constraint, so full jest execution is unverified).
- **Pre-existing repo issue (not from my changes):** root `tsconfig.json` uses `"lib": "ESNext"` (string), which crashes `get-tsconfig` — breaking `npm run lint` for any file with an unresolvable import, and TS 5.9.3 flags it as TS5024. Untouched per constraints; you may want to fix it to `"lib": ["ESNext"]` separately.
